postconditions.satisfied_by: Read global-crew.md, global-everyone.md, g3-implementer-handoff-utf8b.md in full, tests/test_mcp_imperative_equivalence.py's cli_current_text() (line 176-188, one bare subprocess.run(text=True) call, no encoding), checklist_engine.py's _utf8_stdio() (line 43-55, invoked unconditionally at module import line 55 -- CLI child's OWN stdout/stderr always pinned to UTF-8 on the encode side, before PYTHONIOENCODING or any other env var could matter). Empirically confirmed (python3 -c checks, not assumed): locale.getencoding() -- what subprocess.py's _text_encoding() uses for text=True with no explicit encoding -- returns UTF-8 on this box by default AND is unaffected by PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252 set in the shell env (tested directly: still reports UTF-8). PYTHONIOENCODING only governs a NEW interpreter's own sys.stdin/stdout/stderr at startup (why it worked for g3fix2's server-side fix), not subprocess.py's pipe-decode default in the calling process. This box has no cp1252 locale installed (locale -a: only C/C.utf8/POSIX/en_*.utf8) so the true bug (decode default = cp1252) cannot be reproduced by env manipulation alone; m1's demonstration decodes real captured bytes with encoding="cp1252" directly instead, which is the honest, directly-controlled way to prove what an unconfigured Windows box's default would do to these exact production bytes. Handoff verified complete: task, scope (tests/test_mcp_imperative_equivalence.py only), exclusions (no imperative/template/engine edits, no normalising/folding/stripping non-ASCII, no settings.json/checklist JSON/episodes/ edits), required evidence (red-then-green demonstration, local-vs-reasoned split), test mode (fix + sweep + baseline), stop conditions, return format (IMPLEMENTER_RESULT at named path) -- nothing missing.
